goal: Contrast physically different self-portrait capture mechanisms without treating titles as pixel observations
method: Nine live Commons source pages checked for EXIF, original dimensions, uploader, upload revisions and captions; NO new pixel-level inspections

comparisons.inference: Mirror selfie can be captured with interchangeable-lens cameras or a short-focal-length mobile-type camera; camera geometry must be specified, not guessed from 'selfie'.

comparisons.evidence: author captions identify ceiling mirror, outdoor traffic mirror, broken mirror with HDR
comparisons.inference: Reflector curvature/orientation/surface continuity are distinct causal parameters; no visual geometry measurements yet.

comparisons.evidence: C057 photograph made 2015, black-white processed upload 2021; C063 analog 1973 self-portrait uploaded 2024
comparisons.inference: Inception date, upload date, editing date and modern-style suitability must be separate.

falsifiable_tests: Compare ceiling vs planar mirror reflection using actual image pixels and check whether reflected camera orientation follows surface geometry.
Inspect the 2015 edited selfie revisions to determine what contrast/tone changed, without assuming black-and-white is camera-native.
Compare DSLR mirror self-portrait with 2025 low-light hotel mirror portrait to identify focal perspective and noise effects while controlling for scene.
